subject: design-technology
title: Applications: Gears, Pulleys and Cams
welcome_lead: Spin into the world of gears, belts and cams that change speed, torque and motion.
meta_desc: Apply gear ratios, pulleys and cams to working mechanisms.
final_note: You can calculate gear ratios and identify cam profiles by shape.

concepts.def: Toothed wheel that meshes with another to transmit force.
Driven teeth divided by driver teeth.
Wheel with a belt used to transmit rotation.
Shaped wheel that converts rotation into rise and fall.

walkthroughs.body_html: The gear ratio is the number of teeth on the driven gear divided by the teeth on the driver. A high ratio multiplies torque but slows rotation. A 60-tooth driven and 20-tooth driver give a ratio of 3:1 — three times the torque, one third the speed.
Pulleys use belts rather than meshed teeth. A small driver pulley turning a large driven pulley reduces speed and increases torque, the same as gears. Belts are quieter and absorb shock but can slip.
A toy duck needs a smooth up-and-down nodding head. A pear cam gives an even rise and fall. A theatre prop that drops suddenly would use a snail cam — slow build-up, dramatic drop.
